bullets: VyADrwRPJz8 game 3 of 7 (video time 426.6-687.7s), top-ladder, won in overtime. Ryley describes the list as a pressure deck rather than a classic bait deck: "I just like to keep bridge spamming with this man. I think you guys have noticed already that this deck is just complete bridge spam. I wasn't kidding at all when I said there is so much spamming the bridge with this" (450-458s).

The engine is Evo Goblin Barrel + Evo Wall Breakers thrown at whichever tower is cheaper to answer, backed by a Magic Archer at the bridge: ten Goblin Barrels and nine Wall Breakers in 260 readable seconds, and "He has very good goblin barrel answers. But it's not going to be easy to defend the entire game long obviously especially when we start going for things like magic archer at the bridge" (532-540s).

Defence is a fixed shape: Bomb Tower on the (8-9, 8-11) block in front of the King Tower every cycle, Royal Delivery for swarms and the Royal Ghost, and Ice Spirit / Fire Spirit / Berserker as the cheap tops. He explicitly refuses to over-defend - "if he goes for the ram rider, we have the berserker plus ice spirit here just to help take this out. There's no point to drop anything else" (509-513s).

Its currency is forced answers rather than tower damage: "We can barrel wall breakers cuz he has to barbarian barrel that. Yep, perfect ... we forced out snowball as well. That's honestly probably even better than just grabbing the shot that we would have gotten" (618-628s). In overtime that ground the enemy left tower from 2565 to 340 HP between t=600 and t=684 - "Great win" (686s).

Stated fragility: the spirits carry too much of the deck - "this deck is going to get so heavily affected by the nerf to the spirits, man. But it's all good" (479-485s); and the barrel placement is only free while the opponent has no Tornado (436-466s).

new_deck.rationale: Evo Goblin Barrel plus Evo Wall Breakers, Ice Spirit and Fire Spirit exist to drag out small spells and swarm answers (bait), but Ryley pilots them as continuous two-lane bridge pressure with Berserker and Magic Archer rather than as a stall-and-punish list.
new_deck.why_it_works_md: Every offensive card is cheap enough to throw on cycle, so the opponent is answering a 2- or 3-elixir threat with a spell or a swarm placement several times a minute. Ryley's own framing is that the deck wins by taxing rather than by connecting: forcing out an Evo Giant Snowball or a Barbarian Barrel is "probably even better than just grabbing the shot that we would have gotten" (624-628s). Defensively it is very rigid and therefore cheap to pilot - Bomb Tower always in front of the King Tower, Royal Delivery for swarms and ghosts, a spirit or the Berserker on top - which leaves almost all remaining elixir for the opposite lane. The Magic Archer is the pressure valve that makes the barrels un-ignorable, since answering him at the bridge costs more than he does. Its two weak points in this match were the reliance on 1-elixir spirits for defence and the fact that the barrel's default placement is only safe while the opponent is known to have no Tornado.
